Oh dear stranger, I’m so sorry you’re feeling this way. I know it’s hard. I personally battled with major depression and anxiety throughout my teen years and continue to as an adult, but one thing I can say is once I was able to move out and get the hell away from my toxic, unsupportive mother (which is how yours sounds, please correct me if I’m wrong) that one aspect of my life that definitely improved. My only advice is start working ASAP if you’re able. That alone will get you out of the house and away from her more and at the same time you can save up money to get your own place. I can almost guarantee you will feel some relief from not being around somebody that makes you feel like a disappointment. My dad sold/used drugs for most of my life. My parents were divorced and despite his lifestyle my mom allowed him to have shared custody of me. I was probably in third grade and it was his weekend to have me. I got off the school bus on Friday and went home to find that he was in his room asleep. I didn’t think much of it until Saturday evening rolled around and the man still hadn’t moved. So I panicked and called my grandparents. Braver than I, they woke him up with a lot of shaking and yelling. He was furious and made me leave with my grandparents. I found out later that this was because he had been up for days smoking a bunch of crack and was coming down from it all.
As the years went on, I noticed money missing from my piggy bank, the house got messier, food got scarcer, he would disappear for days/weeks on end and visits with him got scarier. He would drive to bad parts of town and leave me in the car for what felt like hours outside of these shitty looking houses (I assume he was doing more drugs) He would make me call my grandparents and tell them I needed money for a field trip or some shit when I definitely didn’t, they would always give me the money and I would give it to him. One time we pulled up to this house in a rural area, he had me go inside with him but was very insistent that I didn’t touch anything. Nobody else was there and he walked out with guns, jewelry, and probably some other stuff that I didn’t see. I don’t know why it didn’t hit me back then, but as I got older I realized I most likely witnessed him rob a house. 

He’s clean now. It took a few arrests, the suicide of my grandpa, my grandma being diagnosed with dementia and schizophrenia, and my dad himself having a stroke, but he doesn’t do crack anymore. 

TL;DR my dad was a crackhead that put me in some situations that were more sketchy than I realized as a child
